records.query: Need the patient's chest X-ray report and pericardial fluid analysis results to determine whether pulmonary congestion is present and to identify the etiology of the pericardial effusion with tamponade physiology, which may be the actual cause of the exertional dyspnea and fatigue rather than heart failure from rapid AF.

Need the patient's ECG, chest X-ray, echocardiography, and B-type natriuretic peptide results, as these are core examinations to confirm heart failure secondary to rapid atrial fibrillation, assess cardiac structure and function, and exclude alternative causes such as pulmonary embolism or exacerbation of pulmonary disease.

CT angiogram and non-contrast CT:     Image Title: Chest, abdomen, and pelvis CT     Image Description: High-density anterior pericardial effusion measuring approximately 3.8 cm in thickness, mild compression of the right lateral ventricle, and reflux of contrast material into the hepatic veins  3. records.query: Need the detailed Doppler echocardiogram findings, including respiratory variation in mitral and tricuspid inflow and inferior vena cava plethora, to confirm tamponade physiology and distinguish it from decompensated heart failure in the setting of rapid AF.

Need the chest CT report and pericardiocentesis fluid analysis results, as these are critical to confirm high-density hemorrhagic pericardial effusion and directly verify warfarin-related hemopericardium while excluding alternative etiologies.

bindings.label: Shortness of breath and fatigue on exertion for one week
Patient is an 84-year-old man with medical history of permanent atrial fibrillation on warfarin therapy for more than 15 years, hypertension, and obstructive sleep apnea.
Patient used a walker for ambulation and had a mechanical fall two years ago with a T12 vertebral fracture requiring orthopedic intervention, with no falls since then.
Medications included metoprolol, amlodipine, and over-the-counter acetaminophen.

Physical examination: blood pressure 140/80 mm Hg, pulse irregular at 130 beats/min, respiratory rate and oxygen saturation normal, jugular venous pressure estimated at 10 cm, heart sounds demonstrated variable intensity of S1 and S2, no murmurs, gallops, or rubs appreciated, remainder unremarkable.
